record.title: Default JWT SECRET_KEY stays accepted whenever ENVIRONMENT is not production
record.description: The production validator refuses weak SECRET_KEY values, SQLite, and empty CORS_ORIGINS, but only after ENVIRONMENT is production or prod. Settings still default SECRET_KEY to the public placeholder change-me-dev-secret, Dockerfile.api/Procfile do not set SECRET_KEY or ENVIRONMENT, and DEPLOY.md first-time order deploys the API with ENVIRONMENT=development then publishes a domain. If that bootstrap (or a forgotten ENVIRONMENT flip) is live and SECRET_KEY was left unset or set to a documented placeholder, an internet caller can HS256-sign staff JWTs with that key. user_from_access_token still requires a matching active User row (UUID sub plus account_id); the break is issuer impersonation for those existing rows, including re-signing a leaked or expired payload. Live Railway env values were not observed.
record.claimed_root_cause: production_must_be_safe is skipped for any non-production ENVIRONMENT, while the in-image default SECRET_KEY and backend/.env.example placeholder remain valid in that mode, and deploy docs start the public API in that mode.

trace.description: Documented first deploy sets ENVIRONMENT=development on the API so CORS_ORIGINS is not required; the same order then uses a public API URL and later flips to production.
SECRET_KEY defaults to the well-known placeholder change-me-dev-secret when unset. .env.example is not loaded; the image has no .env.
If environment is not production or prod, the function returns without rejecting weak keys, SQLite, or missing CORS_ORIGINS.
Access tokens are HS256-signed with settings.secret_key and carry sub, account_id, and role with no audience or issuer.
jwt.decode accepts HS256 with settings.secret_key, require_sub, and verify_aud False, then loads User by payload sub plus account_id.

evidence.description: Env template sets SECRET_KEY=change-me, which production_must_be_safe would reject only after ENVIRONMENT=production.
ENVIRONMENT defaults to development, so is_production is false unless the host overrides it.
Weak-key set includes empty, change-me, and change-me-dev-secret, plus any secret shorter than 32 characters.
After a valid signature, authentication still requires User.id==sub and User.account_id==account_id and an active Account.
The later variables table asks for a long SECRET_KEY, but that check is not enforced until ENVIRONMENT is switched to production.
After the variables table, the API service is told to Generate domain, making the development-mode bind public.

blockers: No OS-enforced sandbox is available (empty allowlist env, no-network namespace, read-only target, trusted parent-side no-follow promotion), so a local dummy JWT forge against the default key was not executed.
Live Railway API ENVIRONMENT and SECRET_KEY were not observed; this run must not probe Railway.
Whether the operator already set a long random SECRET_KEY during the development bootstrap is a host-dashboard fact.

validation_plan.local: In an isolated empty-env sandbox with no backend/.env, start the FastAPI app with ENVIRONMENT=development and SECRET_KEY unset. Seed one dummy Account and User. Mint an HS256 token with key change-me-dev-secret for that user's id and account_id (and a second token for a non-existent pair). Confirm user_from_access_token returns the seeded user for the first token and raises 401 for the second. Repeat startup with ENVIRONMENT=production and unset SECRET_KEY and confirm Settings() raises ValueError before the server binds.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner inspects the Railway API service variables only: if ENVIRONMENT is not production/prod, or SECRET_KEY equals a documented placeholder or is shorter than 32 characters, treat the issue as live. Do not send traffic to the public hostname.
